newsitem.title: SPAIN: Sprint seen in bid for Spain's Retevision.
newsitem.headline: Sprint seen in bid for Spain's Retevision.

text.p: U.S. telephone operator Sprint Corp is expected to join the sole consortium that has expressed interest in acquiring 60 percent of Retevision, which will become the second telephone operator in Spain, a spokesman for the consortium said on Tuesday.
"We are in conversations with various groups but I can confirm that it is anticipated that Sprint will join our alliance in the coming days," the spokesman for the consortium said.
The consortium, which comprises Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG, has said it was interested in bidding for 60 percent of the state's stake in Retevision.
Sprint is already allied with two of these groups in Global One, a European-headquartered venture it owns with France Telecom and with Deutsche Telekom.
Declarations of interest in bidding are due on Monday. If the government accepts the bidder, bids are due by June 9.

The spokesman added that progress had been made in talks with state railway Renfe, which could bring its network of 13,000 km (8,000 miles) of fibre-optic cable to Retevision, which already has its own digital network of 18,000 km of routes and 100,000 km of circuits.
The spokesman also said there were talks with energy utilities Enagas and Endesa, which recently said it would be interested in Retevision's privatisation.
The spokesman did not give any details on the state of talks to form a wider pact and limited himself to saying that time was pressing, given that bids must be handed in on Monday.
On April 3, the government published conditions for the sale in which 2.4 million shares of Retevision out of a total four million will be offered at a minimum price of 45.6 billion pesetas.

The prospective buyer must make a commitment to underwrite another 10 percent capital increase in Retevision. Given a minimum price of 19,000 pesetas per share, the commitment would mean a further expenditure of 25.53 billion pesetas.
After the capital increase, the state will retain a diluted 30 percent stake, a spokesman said.
The period for the presentation of bids concludes on June 9, and Retevision's leadership has committed itself to resolving the placement in 60 days.
